{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Frew Donald McMillan (born 20 May 1942) is a former professional male tennis player from South Africa who won five major doubles championships including three Wimbledons with Bob Hewitt.","title":"Frew McMillan"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Altogether, he won 63 doubles titles, surpassed only by the Bryan brothers, Todd Woodbridge, John McEnroe and Tom Okker.","title":"Frew McMillan"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" He was also ranked No.1 in Doubles on the ATP Computer for a significant period from 1977 to 1979 when he was aged 37.","title":"Frew McMillan"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Tom O'Hare (born 1943 in Mayobridge, County Down) is a former Northern Irish sportsperson.","title":"Tom O'Hare"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" He played Gaelic football with his local clubs Mayobridge and Clonduff and was a member of the Down senior inter-county team from the 1960s until the 1970s.","title":"Tom O'Hare"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" O'Hare won an All-Ireland winners' medal with Down in 1968 scoring two points from 45's.","title":"Tom O'Hare"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Tom was recognised as one of the best defenders ever to play Gaelic football.","title":"Tom O'Hare"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" He is currently a trustee and vice president of his club Mayobrisge.","title":"Tom O'Hare"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" Tom was named on the respected and famous Mícheál Ó Muircheartaigh's team of his life which was published in the Sunday Independent.","title":"Tom O'Hare"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":"noanswer","question":"What county was Tom Hewitt born in?"}
